content.title: HTML Is Structure
content.hook: You already know that the browser turns information into a page the user can see.
content.context:
Now we need to give the browser a more precise description of that page.

HTML is the language we use to describe the **structure and meaning of web content**.

Think of a plain note:

```text
Forge
Learn frontend engineering.
Start learning
```

A human can look at that and guess what is important. HTML gives the browser explicit structure instead of making the browser guess.
goals: Understand that HTML gives a page structure by describing pieces of content and what those pieces are.

content.title: What is an element?
content.text:
An **element** is one structured piece of HTML. For example: ```html

Learn frontend engineering.

``` Here the element says: “This piece of content is a paragraph.” The parts are: - `

` — the opening tag - `Learn frontend engineering.` — the content - `

` — the closing tag Put together, they form a paragraph element.

content.title: Structure is not decoration
content.text:
HTML is not mainly about making text “look right.” Its first job is to describe what the content **is**.

A page can contain a heading, a paragraph, a list, a link, an image, or a form. HTML gives each piece a meaningful place in the document.

content.question:
A learner says: “HTML is just a way to make text appear on a page.”

Which answer corrects the model?

options.text: HTML describes the structure and meaning of content; appearance is a separate concern.

feedback.correct: A useful HTML model starts with structure and meaning, not decoration.
